steps: NSAID (e.g. ibuprofen) + COLCHICINE for ~3 months (reduces recurrence).
Add gastroprotection; restrict strenuous activity until resolved.
Treat the underlying cause; reserve steroids for specific indications (refractory, autoimmune).
Investigate for tamponade if hypotensive/raised JVP.

drugRefs.duration: 1–2 weeks then taper on symptom/CRP resolution
drugRefs.why: First-line anti-inflammatory for acute pericarditis pain; aspirin preferred if concurrent ischaemic heart disease.

drugRefs.dose: 0.5 mg once daily (<70 kg) or twice daily (≥70 kg)
drugRefs.why: Added to the NSAID — improves symptom resolution and roughly halves recurrence.

disposition: Outpatient if low-risk; admit if effusion/high-risk.
